messages.author: 112aae461be3fed5
messages.subject: ggplot2 - plotting error for R3.03
parts:
Hi, 
Here is an example R code that uses ggplot2, I've taken this example from the official ggplot2 documentation:
http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3.1/geom_point.html

> library(ggplot2)
> p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt))
> p = p + geom_point(colour="grey50", size = 4)
> p = p + geom_point(aes(colour = cyl))
> print(p)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : lazy-load database 'P' is corrupt
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In eval(expr, envir, enclos) :
  restarting interrupted promise evaluation
2: In eval(expr, envir, enclos) : internal error -3 in R_decompress1

I always get the same error message with this R version:

> R.version
               _                           
platform       x86_64-pc-linux-gnu         
arch           x86_64                      
os             linux-gnu                   
system         x86_64, linux-gnu           
status                                     
major          3                           
minor          0.3                         
year           2014                        
month          03                          
day            06                          
svn rev        65126                       
language       R                           
version.string R version 3.0.3 (2014-03-06)
nickname       Warm Puppy    

I've tried it on R.14.1 and R3.0.0- no issues. Any ideas what  I'm doing wrong? Is it just this R version? I would like to stay with 
the newer R version, that's why I'm asking for help. Thx for any advice!

Best,

Thx a lot for posting your example. I tried running the example in an R command line session (meaning terminal), no problems. 
I was using R Studio, so I restarted the R session and now it works just fine,...I probably had some preloaded variables/packages still in my 
R environment, I don't know, I should have checked before. (Btw I installed R from the Ubuntu repository, so a simple sudo apt-get install R
and ggplot2 via CRAN)

Thx again! 

Best, 
F.
